label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Sunshine Slack Country
reports.comment:
quick: Stuck to short, mellow sloped laps, with very minimal consequence and no terrain traps, steady runout grade.
Snowpack varied from 90cm to 140cm. The approach from resort and along Wawa ridge had some serious collapse under weight due to the hard surface crust. Could be of some concern on steeper slopes with the snow that day and any future accumulation. Soft powder and good conditions on re…

reports.title: SSV alpine / divide
reports.comment: quick: SSV meadows and surrounding terrain entirely facetted with occasional wind slabs - had a few settlements even on low angle terrain. A few Na 1.5+ on E aspect at 2300m per pic that scrubbed to ground. Definitely will make for a weak base later this season when snow builds up. HS varies from 15-40cm and boot pen to ground unless on slab.

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows / quartz
reports.comment: quick: An encouraging improvement in conditions the last 24hrs with the arrival of 25cm of dry, low density snow.  Average HS 50 to 60cm,  ski pen 25 or to ground.  Whumphing was constant, large and widespread with trailbreaking on all features.  Probably the lowest snowpack for this time of year on the divide ive seen in 30 years.  Wx partly cloudy, winds calm, -10C at 10:00, -8C at noon.

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Lots of new snow in the Sunshine area. Good conditions on the trail in, fast on the way out.  Dug a pit on a south aspect, about 600m east of Healy Pass at 2244m. 54cm HS and 20cm storm snow on a weak base. Column test, no results. Supportive enough to ski but still plenty of rocks lurking.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: We went up to the Wawa ridge from top of the chair to just below the repeater. Ski down SE bowl to 2250m then traverse back to ski hill. Up to 25cm F recent storm snow overlies either MFcr or hard wind slab. Average HS is 50cm, still thin coverage overall. SH grows up to 3cm at tree line and sheltered alpine. Observed whumpfing in the forest.

reports.title: Wawa bump
reports.comment:
snowpack: Dug out at 2370m. HS 36, 1-2mm SH on surface, first resistance facets to 14cm, 3mm Depth hoar below. 

CTE 5 down 22 on DH - break
CTE 6 down 20 on DH - break

reports.title: The Little Gem ice climb.
reports.comment:
quick: Took the old tools for a walk up to The little Gem. Didn’t climb it due to a later than anticipated start and time constraints.

It’s a good 3 hour approach from the trail head. There’s a path punched in now. 

I would not want to be in this zone after then next snowfall. 

The approach goes through challenging avalanche terrain. Lots of evidence of large slides in the approach drainage. 

…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Skinned to ridge top for some fitness and to shake off the early season rust. Skied the mellow slope on skiers right of the main bowl, some good turns to be had but the rocks remind you they’re still there every couple of turns. “Skied” the backdoor drainage back to the resort, not recommended… / snowpack: Dug a test pit on the approach to the ridge. ECTP20 down 38cm on 3mm basal DH.

reports.title: Wawa
reports.comment: quick: Not a ton to update. Conditions remains mostly below threshold. Definitely more likely to be injured catching a shark than in an avalanche. Tips up and careful riding! Widespread surface hoar near treeline. Some small sluffing in steep thin terrain.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Wawa ridge on Sunday. Overall good snow. Coverage is improving compared to beginning of the season but hazards are still present. Snow depth varied from 12-50+ centimetres in some places. The integrity of the base + incoming storm + winds encouraged us to be conservative with our lines. The top of the ridge was windy with poor visibility but relatively good coverage allowed easy mobility. R…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Skiied a few laps off Wawa ridge, snow depth anywhere from 10-50cm but generally found it on the deeper side in most places. Very windy at ridgetop with lots of wind transport happening, but didn't see any signs of instability aside from a thin windskin sending some shooting cracks.

Dug a few hand shears in the alpine (E facing slopes), the blocks tended to just fall apart with no distinct…

reports.title: Wawa ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Couple of laps off Wawa ridge climbers left just above the resort.  Boot top powder.  There was already a beaten in skin track from Thursday? but only one set of down tracks.

Approx 1m of snow. Quite a few whoompfs crossing the flats to / from the resort.

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: It was a mostly cloudy day never warming up above -12c. At our maximum elevation around 2300 meters there was definite whumping occurring on mellow terrain. 90 cms base with 45+ cms new snow.

reports.title: SSV slack
reports.comment:
quick: Went for a bit of exploration in the slack country. Found amazing boot top powder everywhere outside the boundary, but given avy hazard we didn’t ride anything steep enough to be actually ski, minus about 15 good turns off the backside of Standish. 

Dug a pit there, HS around 85cm with the bottom being the nicely faceted section. Column test failed after 3 shoulder taps straight on the gro…

reports.title: Grizzly glades
reports.comment: quick: Great skiing in the trees and mellow slopes, skied only east aspects, one remote trigger sz 1.5, initial fracture propagated 25-30 meters, slid approximately 40 meters. Dug a quick RB prior to first descent, storm layer slid at RB3 and deep persistent layer was quite stubborn with very little movement. Noticed several short debris paths on west aspects which popped during the storm. / avala…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: We went for a tour up to Healy Pass today and skied very conservative terrain. Variable conditions were present due to wind affect, but areas that weren’t crusted contained excellent dry powder and made for some great skiing! / snowpack: We dug a pit (not full size) and completed a quick compression test with a CT26 sudden drop result on the interface between a 5cm thick crust and facets at…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge & Standish tour
reports.comment: quick: A nice early season tour up Wawa Ridge and Standish.  We were able to skin all the way to the summit of the ridge (I've never been able to do that before, usually have to boot pack the last 100m).  Skiing was much better than expected, we enjoyed some good turns on great powder down mellow slopes below the ridge.   We stayed entirely out of avalanche terrain, but noted no instabilities desp…

reports.title: Quartz hill
reports.comment:
quick: Variable HS on the NW aspect of the false summit of Quartz hill. There were heavily wind affected areas on ridges and away from trees, the small slopes that could slide were forming small cookies that popped off. / weather: Very variable wind direction. Limited solar inputs on the day. Near end of day (1530 hrs) fog was present and obscuring visibility. 
Air temp was between -4.8 C and -6.2…

reports.title: Bear Sprit Approach
reports.comment: avalanche: On our hike out from Bear Spirit, we observed the aftermath a wet slab that ran over the approach trail. Foliage was scarce so i assume this slides occasionally. It ran to ground and the deposit was about a meter in depth where it crossed the trail. 9am temps at the car where around 2 degrees and were about the same when we returned around 3pm. It felt warmer in this area of the approac…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge Laps
reports.comment: quick: Great day skiing the front side of Wawa ridge. We skinned up all the way to the top of the ridge, which was quite wind affected. We skied below the ridge, out of the wind. Light powder made for a really fun day and some great turns.

reports.title: Healy pass
reports.comment:
quick: supportive crust 20-40cm below surface.
observed large cornices on Monarch ramparts and the track of a size 1 avalanche on steep windload NE slopes. 
Good coverage, no rocks hit.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Toured up the Sunshine ski out and topped out at the top of Wawa Ridge. Snow conditions varied depending on where you were during the climb. Snow pack felt dense and firm under foot. Walked part of the ridge to get up, very wind affected and packed down. Made for an easy walk. Skiing was ok, lots of people have made turns here so the area is a bit skied out. However, still soft snow to be f…

reports.title: Goat's Eye - Profile
reports.comment:
quick: Before doing the profile, we toured around Wawa Ridge - 10 cm ski penetration at treeline, generally supportive snowpack to skis, isolated wind slabs found around Wawa ridge - stubbornly reactive and not propagating on the one feature we tested.  We didn't travel far, so only a point observation.

In the Goat's Eye profile, we found a gradual temperature gradient and evidence of rounding & …

reports.title: Monarch Ramparts
reports.comment: quick: Went up Healy and across the ramparts to Eohippus. Snow was moist up to 2000m at 13:30. Winds moderate gusting strong from the sw at ridgetop with moderate wind transport. On sheltered or NE aspects there was 10-20 of fist on-top of old 4 and 1 finger windslabs with a crust down 50 and then facets to ground. Average hs at TL was 90. Ridgetop was scoured and cornices were still small. Not a …

reports.title: Healy/Monarch
reports.comment: quick: Beautiful bluebird day at Healy Pass bordering on Monarch Ramparts. We only skied east-facing slopes and mostly stuck to trees and a few chutes. Total snow depth was 80-100cm below treeline. Snow was fairly soft and uniform throughout and made for great skiing. It is still shallow enough to be concerned about rocks and other features below the surface. Above treeline the snow was much thinn…

reports.title: Big V, Central peak
reports.comment:
quick: Dropped down to Healy via 2nd drainage, no signs of instability, snow was better than expected 
Skied up Y drainage, travel was difficult, needs another 12-24” to cover downfall 
Cut a cornice into the big V, entrained some recent wind deposed snow travelling down 100m, did not propagate sideways or step down.
Skied a run on central peak NE side, very wind affected even low down
Exit via bi…

reports.title: Wawa to the creek
reports.comment:
quick: No whumpfs or cracks in any walking. 
Slopes below 35 degrees help up well with very little wind slab development in treeline and below treeline.

Hs was consistently 80-90 cm at 2300M

Air temps consistently throughout the day at -4 degrees. Still treading lightly over the basal facets that are definitely still present.

reports.title: Healy pass
reports.comment: quick: Walked up to Healy pass today. Snow pack surprisingly normal with 60cm of increasing consolidation, then 20-30cm of facets. Great turns up at the pass. There was wind effect on the pass ridge but staying a couple hundred meters away lead to some fun turns. Ski pen 20cm, boot pen 80cm+.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Toured out from the Wawa lift onto some slopes on Wawa ridge and on the shoulders of Twin Carines. Snow was soft and buttery with a firmer layer below on leeward slopes but harder and wind effected on windward slopes. No signs of instability or avalanche. The weather all day was mostly cloudy with very light dusting of snow, light wind, and patches of fog at higher elevations for most of th…

reports.title: Healy Pass/Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Skied hippie trees by Healy Pass. Snow was soft and playful, had spectacular views of sunshine and a bit of scarab peak poked out.

Dug a small profile and found plenty of facets at the base. The temperature crust is very supportive and appears to be bridging the load of skiers, but I wouldn’t count on it being the case everywhere, especially when getting onto higher elevations or northern …

reports.title: Spray River Falls
reports.comment:
quick: Spray River Falls has seen enough traffic that there is a well trodden trail to the base of the climb. There are options to avoid a fair bit of the gully by utilizing game trails on the ridge either side. We were 1:40 to the base. Micro-spikes are recommended.
P1: 35m on WI3 to a screw/V-thread anchor. Hike 70m to the base of the main ice flow.
P2: 30m on WI3/4 to a screw/V-thread anchor if…

reports.title: Lots of settlement at 2400m
reports.comment:
quick: Lapped Grizzly trees multiple times. Lots of wind effect at treeline and alpine circa 2350m and higher. Had at least 15 settlements at treeline in open terrain on the basal layers and then stopped counting. Treeline was a mix of wind skin, crust and slab. Made for hooky skiing. S facing trees skied great - snow was supportive but not as fast as expected (still quite cold).

Didn’t trigger a…

reports.title: Whumpfing around Healy Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Observed an impressive amount of whumfing and settlements while touring around the Healy Pass area today.

Unsurprisingly, some quick digging in the snow revealed extensive facetting in the base of the snowpack.

We stayed on <30 slopes.

reports.title: Conservative day out
reports.comment:
quick: Taking into consideration other MIN reports and the danger rating bulletins, we rode mellow slopes below treeline. 

We moved quickly through the avalanche path runouts and kept an eye on risks above us. 

We didn’t experience any whumpfs or cracks but stayed fairly low.

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment: quick: The pack settled at least 10 times on us.  Very touchy and glad to avoid most slopes.

reports.title: Healy Pass - Prime avalanche conditions
reports.comment: quick: We chose healy pass as it is our go to for considerable days as you can mostly avoid avalanche terrain (aside from the 3 runouts that must be passed on the trail in). We dug a pit on a southern representative aspect with a slope of about 26 degrees. We immediately noticed some very concerning layers in the snowpack. About 30cm of harder snow sitting on two separate facet layers. We got prop…

reports.title: Secondary Drain, Storm slabs all elevations
reports.comment: quick: Around noon the sun came out and temperatures rapidly warmed up to 0C at Treeline and below. From the the top of Wawa hump to Healy Creak Trail we found cakey storm slabs 20cm deep sitting on facets from the warm temperatures today and yesterday.   Trail breaking and skiing were difficult, with hooky snow.  The slabs didn't feel very reactive but we were glad that are route stayed less than…

reports.title: Monarch Rampart
reports.comment: quick: A warm day going up to the Ramparts. We avoided all avi slopes to reach the ridge, which was wind scoured. LOTS of whumpfing, but always on flat spots, never on a slope. No shooting cracks, so the weak layer was reactive and settling but not really seeing propagation. Good snow on the descent on mellow slopes. Need to go back in better conditions.

reports.title: Sunshine landing
reports.comment: quick: With considerable avalanche hazard we skinned up to Sunshine Landing for a low risk day. We heard several whomps and stayed on low angle terrain

reports.title: SSV meadows test pit
reports.comment: quick: Whumpfing and settlements, upon inspection this is going on the Arctic facets around 25-30 down. Basal facets are still able to be triggered but are secondary in this area.

reports.title: Sunshine Landing Jan 30
reports.comment: quick: The snow in the Sunshine meadows was crusty and wind affected. We did not have any whumpfing or cracks. There was a recent avalanche on the south side of Brewster Rock likely caused by a cornice failure, and saw some recent activity on many slopes, including Bourgeau.

reports.title: Wawa ridge pits
reports.comment:
quick: Skied up Wawa ridge to assess conditions and dug 3 pits.

Widespread breakable crust, occasionally supportive to skis depending on aspect. Ski pen 10-20cm when breaking through crust. Foot pen to ground most places. Ski quality is terrible. Snowpack moist to base.

Top 17-25cm 1F resistance moist slab composed of 1mm rounding facets. 

Fist resistance facets beneath. Compression tests, and …

reports.title: Spray River Falls
reports.comment: quick: 5cm of evenly distributed  storm snow overlying a breakable melt-freeze crust was observed on the hike in. As soon as the sun came out spindrift started to come down from the steep rocky ledges on the left and right side of the climb and continued throughout the day. Seven or so were noted and five of these swept over the climb directly, running fast and loose over the melt freeze crust. Th…

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment: quick: We found good skiing on planar low angle slopes between 2400m and 2100m. Snow was nice and fast. Moderate south winds were building wind slabs on lee alpine features.  As soon as the slope angle was steep or variable you felt the crust.

reports.title: Bourgeau Meadows, Center Peak
reports.comment:
quick: The crust was not supportive below 2100m and the snow was still slightly moist below the new snow.  15cm of storm snow make for good turns on mellow slopes were you won't hit the crust underneath. Crust was bigger on solar alpine slopes but less than 1cm think on polar aspects below 2550m.  small wind slabs on at the top of ridge crest and not extending more than 20m down slope.  

We had w…

reports.comment:
quick: The crust was not supportive below 2100m and the snow was still slightly moist below the new snow.  15cm of storm snow make for good turns on mellow slopes were you won't hit the crust underneath. Crust was bigger on solar alpine slopes but less than 1cm think on polar aspects below 2550m.  small wind slabs on at the top of ridge crest and not extending more than 20m down slope.

reports.title: Healy Area
reports.comment: quick: Walked around the Healy area, widespread surface hoar up to 4mm from TL and above(smaller in wind affected terrain). Steeper solar slopes at treeline had the top 5cm turning moist, but stayed dry in the alpine. Numerous whumpfs on the thin and wind affected ridgetop of Pyramid Peak, but not on any other ridgetop. Skiing up to 10cm of nice low density pow with a supportive crust below, even …

reports.title: Ready to Rock(ski)
reports.comment: quick: Skied the Goat's Eye, BTL travel was tough, at TL up to 10 of fist snow on top of a supportive crust(made skinning hard). In Alpine the crust was mostly supportive to boots. The main path below the choke had slid previously but the climbers right side had a 10cm 4f windlsab with resistant planar hand shears. Choke was steep with some rock moves. Skied consistent the whole way down, sluff wa…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Skied the Sunshine slackcountry today on the ridge between Wawa and Twin Cairns. Good skiing in the fresh snow on top of the recent crust from last week's warm spell, and plenty of under-equipped folks were hiking out from the resort to take advantage. / snowpack: See profile image.

reports.title: Quartz + SSV slack
reports.comment: quick: Skied Quartz 1 from the col and then did the Twin Cairns traverse S to N. Natural size 1.5 along the Quartz 1 ridge that failed as a cohesive slab, likely from yesterday/overnight wind loading. Saw what appeared to be a recent size 2 where they always deliver on Quartz, where the cornice builds. Interestingly, you can see the recent slab in red, and an old slab in yellow - the bed surface h…

reports.title: Little Fatigue
reports.comment: quick: ECT on N aspect, 2240 elevation, HS 105cm produced failure with full propagation across the column @ 18cm on top of the Feb 3 MFcr. Remainder of the pack was stubborn, with no other instabilities noticed. Mainly facets, depth hoar and crust. Observed 2 slide paths from Cornice failure on N aspect running down to the feb 3 crust. Size 1-1.5. Found good supportive crust for skiing down to 215…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Perfect day at Healy Pass. 20-30cm of faceting powder on top of a supportive crust. Travel BTL was fine, if slow on the way out. No wind slabs observed, wind affected snow was seen in the high alpine but didn't go there. Dug a quick pit on a NE slope and observed a 1cm thick crust and essentially only facets above and below it. Did an extended column test which had no results, even when I t…

reports.title: The Needle - Talc
reports.comment:
quick: It was a long day.  27km, 1700m of vert, door to door 9.5hrs. 

We had left at an early hour to make sure we hit the solar aspects as early as possible, although due to cloudy conditions, there was a solar input at times and definitely was looking out for any activity, but non observed.

We chose to ascend the S,SW slope in the burnt trees. Certainly kept in mind the multiple Sz 2/2.5 avala…

reports.title: Rockisle Pit and Quartz Hill
reports.comment: quick: Skied mellow terrain around Rockisle lake and Quartz hill. Saw ~20cm of moist snow on top of Feb 3 crust made for good skiing conditions in sheltered areas. Suncrust forming on steep southern aspects

reports.title: No-Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment: quick: Took the splitboard for a walk into sunshine meadows and rode some low angle slopes. About 10-15cm of powder sitting on a supportive crust.

reports.title: Wawa North Slack Size 2
reports.comment:
quick: Post-work afternoon walk around Wawa North towards Healy Main; no signs of instability nor natural activity. 

On the way towards the drainage, we avoided the steep alpine features leading towards the drain and skied a mellow gully.

When in the gully, we remote triggered (~100m) a size 2 avalanche on a steep cross-loaded alpine feature near tree line. It failed on the DPL. 

We dug a pit i…

reports.title: Cold & Windy Sunshine
reports.comment: quick: High winds made for uncomfortably cold travel in the alpine and a lot of snow moving around forming wind slabs.  No signs of instability, but was also in mellow terrain and visibility was low.  The sustained winds around noon seemed higher than forecasted.

reports.title: Healy Pass Path 2
reports.comment: quick: The Healy Pass second avalanche path went full, didn’t take out the east flank of the path but went down the gut right to the bottom and across the summer trail.

reports.title: Skier accidental size 1 in the Wizard Chutes
reports.comment: avalanche: Skier triggered a small slab and was carried down through trees resulting in minor injuries. The slab appears to have released 60-80 cm down. Suspect it released on the facets above the Feb 3 crust. / incident: Skier triggered a small slab and was carried down through trees resulting in minor injuries. The slab appears to have released 60-80 cm down. Suspect it released on the facets ab…

reports.title: Bear Spirit
reports.comment: quick: Crossed a small avalanche on the approach to Bear Spirit that crossed the trail where the Atlas shows it can.  Looked recent from warming.

reports.title: Above Healy Creek
reports.comment: quick: On SE - SW aspects above Healy creek in the morning the PWL was very chatty. Hard to take a step without it collapsing. On a few tight kickturns it released and slid slightly on large grain facets ~35cm down. In the afternoon when returning the snow was pretty soggy and was not collapsing in the same way.

reports.title: Sunshine meadows.  Hot
reports.comment: quick: Felt like a late May sunshine day skiing.  Good travel conditions in the Meadows. The south aspects had corn snow in them at tree line and below and skied good away from old wind slabs.  Shallow areas were not very supportive.  Found some powder on north aspects above 2250m.  Many wet loose avalanche in the south facing front ranges and a few slabs pulled out in the alpine.  Hopefully the w…

reports.title: Lower Twin Cairns slopes.
reports.comment: snowpack: Solar input was changing the surface snow. By 11 am the surface snow changed from powder to wet and getting heavy at 2400 meters. Column test on NE aspect 25deg slope.

reports.title: Skier remote Citadel E face
reports.comment: quick: Went for a walk out to citadel pass and ended up ascending Citadel peak. Great travel through the meadows on semi supportive solar crust up to 2cm thick except on N aspects which held dry snow that was supportive to skinning. Solar input was cooking by 11am. A few natural rumbles, quite a bit of debris on all aspects bar North. Definitely still touchy out there so avoid avalanche terrain an…

reports.title: Sulphur slide
reports.comment: avalanche: Wet slide near Sulphur Mountain Hiking trail between 1300-1600hrs. Started from steep rocky cliff bad in trees on se aspect.

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows - Quartz Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly few red flags today, no rollerballs, collapsing, etc. Stayed on really mellow terrain, but encountered a variety of surfaces, the vast majority were still supportive sun crusts till 1pm. Real hot day, down to just the base layer around noon.

reports.title: Buck wild bourg
reports.comment: quick: Summited Bourgeau via Sunshine back lot to Borg meadow and skied Borg 10 to 9.75. Travel was good throughout, supportive crust from bottom to top, finding up to 30 cms of fist in upper tree line, and average of 15-20. On the summit ramp average of 80 cm with a 3 cms pencil  bomber crust with facetes beneath. Good skiing throughout. Some older size 2-3.5 off the solar aspects from warming cy…

reports.title: Quartz Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Went up Quartz Ridge in SSV backcountry as a party of 4 and rode the Col Inbetween Quartz hill summit and Quartz ridge. (2504m) 

Travel up until the start of the ridge traverse was well packed in. Approx 6-12cm of low density snow sitting at top of a supportive crust. (2230m)

Snow below ridge was great and felt stable, up until topping out where the wind effect was highly noticeable. (230…

reports.title: Healy/Lost Horse/Bourgeau Meadows
reports.comment:
quick: Nice touring from Healy area towards Bourgeau meadows. Tried to find softer snow on northern and eastern aspects with minimal success - it appears low angle slopes of all aspects are getting sun-baked at this time of year! 
Winds were moderate-high throughout the day with minimal wind transport due to firmness of snow, thankfully the breeze kept surfaces cool enough to avoid skin stick. Evi…

reports.title: Monarch Ramparts
reports.comment: quick: Plan A of the day was to try Mt Bourgeau, but the coverage below treeline was lower than we had hoped for.  Went for a tour up Monarch Ramparts instead.  Great snow in the alpine still, we enjoyed a steep run down from the ramparts in the late morning.  Good travel conditions all day but deteriorating as expected with wet snow in the afternoon and at lower elevations.  No instabilities note…

reports.title: Mt Bourgeau
reports.comment: quick: Bluebird day climbing and skiing the SW path of Mt Bourgeau today. A bit of wind up high but not bad. The Healy Pass trail still has coverage. S aspects below 2100m are really starting to loose snow coverage; we had to take our skis off repeatedly between Healy creek and that elevation. Perfect 5-10cm powder above 2500m.

reports.title: Goats eye
reports.comment: quick: Went to check out the goats eye thinking we would likely just ski the slide paths. As we got up high the snow felt good underfoot and was bonding very well so we went to the eye. Rock bands were completely covered and we skied deep powder in the chute (20-30cm.) The slide path also skied very well until 1900m. The lower path was moist powder. No signs of instability on ascent or descent in …

reports.title: Wet slabs
reports.comment:
quick: With no over night freeze and day time tempratures  in the low teens in the alpine,  a wet slab avalanche cycle started.  Of note:

Quartz ridge size 2+ wet slab on Ne aspect just south of the summit.

Hawk ridge size 3 wet loose.

Goats eye North aspect had size 2+ wet slab run just above tree line.

Several size 2.5 to 3.5 wet slabs on Rundles north aspect.  

Size 2.5 from the gully betw…
